sanskrit: dīrghakāloṣitas tasmin girau girivanapriyaḥ videhyāḥ priyamākāṅkṣan svaṃ ca cittaṃ vilobhayan
english: Having dwelt long on that mountain, he who delighted in hills and forests, wishing to please the Videhan princess and also to charm his own heart—

sanskrit: atha dāśarathiś citraṃ citrakūṭam adarśayat bhāryām amarasaṃkāśaḥ śacīm iva puraṃdaraḥ
english: —then Daśaratha's son, radiant as an immortal, pointed out the variegated Citrakūṭa to his wife, even as Puraṃdara shows Śacī the wonders of heaven.

sanskrit: na rājyād bhraṃśanaṃ bhadre na suhṛdbhir vinābhavaḥ mano me bādhate dṛṣṭvā ramaṇīyam imaṃ girim
english: "Neither the loss of the kingdom, dear one, nor the separation from friends distresses my mind, for I have seen this delightful mountain."

sanskrit: paśyemam acalaṃ bhadre nānādvijagaṇāyutam śikharaiḥ kham ivodviddhair dhātumadbhir vibhūṣitam
english: "Behold this mountain, dear one, thronged with hosts of many birds, adorned with mineral-streaked peaks that seem to pierce the sky."

sanskrit: ke cid rajatasaṃkāśāḥ ke cit kṣatajasaṃnibhāḥ pītamāñjiṣṭhavarṇāś ca ke cin maṇivaraprabhāḥ
english: "Some regions gleam like silver, some resemble blood-red ochre, some are yellow-madder-coloured, and some shine with the brilliance of precious gems."

sanskrit: puṣyārkaketukābhāś ca ke cij jyotī rasaprabhāḥ virājante 'calendrasya deśā dhātuvibhūṣitāḥ
english: "Some parts blaze like Puṣya's star, like the sun, like Ketuka flowers; some gleam with a liquid luminescence—the slopes of this king of mountains shine forth, adorned with mineral ores."

sanskrit: nānāmṛgagaṇadvīpitarakṣvṛkṣagaṇair vṛtaḥ aduṣṭair bhāty ayaṃ śailo bahupakṣisamākulaḥ
english: "This mountain shines, surrounded by herds of various deer, leopards, bears, and troops of trees—harmless and teeming with multitudes of birds."

sanskrit: āmrajambvasanair lodhraiḥ priyālaiḥ panasair dhavaiḥ aṅkolair bhavyatiniśair bilvatindukaveṇubhiḥ
english: "With mango, rose-apple, Asana, Lodhra, Priyāla, jackfruit, Dhava, Aṅkola, Bhavya, Tiniśa, Bilva, Tinduka, and bamboo—"

sanskrit: kāśmaryariṣṭavaraṇair madhūkais tilakais tathā badaryāmalakair nīpair vetradhanvanabījakaiḥ
english: "—with Kāśmarya, Ariṣṭa, Varaṇa, Madhūka, Tilaka, Badarī, Āmalaka, Nīpa, Vetra, Dhanvana, and Bījaka trees—"

sanskrit: puṣpavadbhiḥ phalopetaiś chāyāvadbhir manoramaiḥ evamādibhir ākīrṇaḥ śriyaṃ puṣyaty ayaṃ giriḥ
english: "—bearing flowers, laden with fruits, providing shade, and delightful—crowded with these and others, this mountain flourishes in its glory."

sanskrit: śailaprastheṣu ramyeṣu paśyemān kāmaharṣaṇān kinnarān dvaṃdvaśo bhadre ramamāṇān manasvinaḥ
english: "On the charming mountain plateaus, dear one, behold these Kinnaras who delight the heart with desire—noble beings sporting in pairs."

sanskrit: śākhāvasaktān khaḍgāṃś ca pravarāṇy ambarāṇi ca paśya vidyādharastrīṇāṃ krīḍed deśān manoramān
english: "Behold the swords hung from branches, the fine garments, and the charming pleasure-spots of Vidyādhara women."

sanskrit: jalaprapātair udbhedair niṣyandaiś ca kva cit kva cit sravadbhir bhāty ayaṃ śailaḥ sravan mada iva dvipaḥ
english: "With cascading waterfalls, with springs breaking forth, with rivulets flowing here and there, this mountain shines like an elephant streaming with ichor."

sanskrit: guhāsamīraṇo gandhān nānāpuṣpabhavān vahan ghrāṇatarpaṇam abhyetya kaṃ naraṃ na praharṣayet
english: "The breeze from the caves, bearing the fragrance born of many flowers, gratifying the sense of smell as it draws near—what person would it not fill with joy?"

sanskrit: yadīha śarado 'nekās tvayā sārdham anindite lakṣmaṇena ca vatsyāmi na māṃ śokaḥ pradhakṣyati
english: "If I were to dwell here many autumns together with you, blameless one, and with Lakṣmaṇa, sorrow would not consume me."

sanskrit: bahupuṣpaphale ramye nānādvijagaṇāyute vicitraśikhare hy asmin ratavān asmi bhāmini
english: "In this peak abounding in flowers and fruits, charming, thronged with various flocks of birds, in this summit of marvellous hues, I have found delight, fair one."

sanskrit: anena vanavāsena mayā prāptaṃ phaladvayam pituś cānṛṇatā dharme bharatasya priyaṃ tathā
english: "Through this forest-dwelling I have obtained a twofold fruit: discharge of my debt of duty to my father, and the fulfilment of Bharata's wish."

sanskrit: vaidehi ramase kaccic citrakūṭe mayā saha paśyantī vividhān bhāvān manovākkāyasaṃyatān
english: "Are you content, Vaidehī, dwelling with me on Citrakūṭa, beholding the varied expressions of those restrained in mind, word, and deed?"

sanskrit: idam evāmṛtaṃ prāhū rājñāṃ rājarṣayaḥ pare vanavāsaṃ bhavārthāya pretya me prapitāmahāḥ
english: "This very life is called nectar by foremost royal sages; my great ancestors proclaimed that the forest-dwelling serves the highest purpose of existence."

sanskrit: śilāḥ śailasya śobhante viśālāḥ śataśo 'bhitaḥ bahulā bahulair varṇair nīlapītasitāruṇaiḥ
english: "The boulders of the mountain shine on all sides in their hundreds—vast, manifold, of manifold colours: blue, yellow, white, and red."

sanskrit: niśi bhānty acalendrasya hutāśanaśikhā iva oṣadhyaḥ svaprabhā lakṣmyā bhrājamānāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: "At night the luminous herbs of this king of mountains shine by their own radiance like tongues of fire, blazing in their glory by the thousands."

sanskrit: ke cit kṣayanibhā deśāḥ ke cid udyānasaṃnibhāḥ ke cid ekaśilā bhānti parvatasyāsya bhāmini
english: "Some regions resemble a palace, some look like pleasure-gardens, and some single great rocks gleam on this mountain, fair one."

sanskrit: bhittveva vasudhāṃ bhāti citrakūṭaḥ samutthitaḥ citrakūṭasya kūṭo 'sau dṛśyate sarvataḥ śivaḥ
english: "Citrakūṭa rises as if having split open the earth; that summit of Citrakūṭa appears auspicious in every direction."

sanskrit: kuṣṭhapuṃnāgatagarabhūrjapatrottaracchadān kāmināṃ svāstarān paśya kuśeśayadalāyutān
english: "Behold the beds spread out for lovers, covered with Kuṣṭha, Puṃnāga, Tagara, Bhūrja leaves, and upper coverings of lotus petals—couch-like and spread out."

sanskrit: mṛditāś cāpaviddhāś ca dṛśyante kamalasrajaḥ kāmibhir vanite paśya phalāni vividhāni ca
english: "Garlands of lotuses, pressed and shot through by bows, are seen scattered by lovers—behold, dear one, the many kinds of fruit lying about as well."

sanskrit: vasvaukasārāṃ nalinīm atyetīvottarān kurūn parvataś citrakūṭo 'sau bahumūlaphalodakaḥ
english: "That mountain Citrakūṭa, abounding in roots, fruits, and water, surpasses even Vasvaukasāra's lotus-lake and the northern Kurus in its abundance."

sanskrit: imaṃ tu kālaṃ vanite vijahrivāṃs tvayā ca sīte saha lakṣmaṇena ca ratiṃ prapatsye kuladharmavardhinīṃ satāṃ pathi svair niyamaiḥ paraiḥ sthitaḥ
english: "Sporting through this season, dear Sītā, together with you and with Lakṣmaṇa, I shall attain that contentment which augments the dharma of our lineage—standing on the path of the good, by my own supreme vows."

sanskrit: atha śailād viniṣkramya maithilīṃ kosaleśvaraḥ adarśayac chubhajalāṃ ramyāṃ mandākinīṃ nadīm
english: Then, descending from the mountain, the lord of Kosala showed the Maithilī princess the charming river Mandākinī with its auspicious waters.

sanskrit: abravīc ca varārohāṃ cārucandranibhānanām videharājasya sutāṃ rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ
english: And Rāma, lotus-eyed, spoke to that daughter of the Videha king, she of noble waist and face fair as a lovely moon:

sanskrit: vicitrapulināṃ ramyāṃ haṃsasārasasevitām kusumair upasaṃpannāṃ paśya mandākinīṃ nadīm
english: "Behold the river Mandākinī—her sandy banks variegated, charming, frequented by geese and cranes, adorned with flowers."

sanskrit: nānāvidhais tīraruhair vṛtāṃ puṣpaphaladrumaiḥ rājantīṃ rājarājasya nalinīm iva sarvataḥ
english: "Encircled by diverse trees growing along her banks—flowering and fruit-bearing—she shines on all sides like the lotus-pool of the king of kings."

sanskrit: mṛgayūthanipītāni kaluṣāmbhāṃsi sāmpratam tīrthāni ramaṇīyāni ratiṃ saṃjanayanti me
english: "The fords, their waters now muddied by herds of deer that have drunk there, are charming and arouse delight in me."

sanskrit: jaṭājinadharāḥ kāle valkalottaravāsasaḥ ṛṣayas tv avagāhante nadīṃ mandākinīṃ priye
english: "At the appointed hour, sages wearing matted locks and antelope-skin, their upper garments of bark-cloth, plunge into the river Mandākinī, dear one."

sanskrit: ādityam upatiṣṭhante niyamād ūrdhvabāhavaḥ ete 'pare viśālākṣi munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
english: "Other ascetics with sharp vows stand with arms raised, worshipping the sun with discipline, wide-eyed one."

sanskrit: mārutoddhūta śikharaiḥ pranṛtta iva parvataḥ pādapaiḥ patrapuṣpāṇi sṛjadbhir abhito nadīm
english: "The mountain seems to dance, its peaks tossed by the wind, its trees scattering leaves and flowers all around the river."

sanskrit: kaccin maṇinikāśodāṃ kaccit pulinaśālinīm kaccit siddhajanākīrṇāṃ paśya mandākinīṃ nadīm
english: "How gem-bright are her waters! How rich in sandbanks! How thronged with Siddhas! Behold the river Mandākinī!"

sanskrit: nirdhūtān vāyunā paśya vitatān puṣpasaṃcayān poplūyamānān aparān paśya tvaṃ jalamadhyagān
english: "Behold the masses of blossoms blown off and spread out by the wind; behold others floating, borne along in the middle of the stream."

sanskrit: tāṃś cātivalgu vacaso rathāṅgāhvayanā dvijāḥ adhirohanti kalyāṇi niṣkūjantaḥ śubhā giraḥ
english: "The cakravāka birds, whose calls are most sweet, cry out auspicious sounds as they mount those flowers—how charming, auspicious one!"

sanskrit: darśanaṃ citrakūṭasya mandākinyāś ca śobhane adhikaṃ puravāsāc ca manye ca tava darśanāt
english: "The sight of Citrakūṭa and of the Mandākinī, radiant one—I deem it greater than dwelling in the city, and greater even than the sight of you alone."

sanskrit: vidhūtakaluṣaiḥ siddhais tapodamaśamānvitaiḥ nityavikṣobhita jalāṃ vihāhasva mayā saha
english: "Come, sport with me in these ever-stirred waters, alongside the Siddhas whose impurities have been shaken off, endowed with austerity, self-restraint, and tranquillity."

sanskrit: sakhīvac ca vigāhasva sīte mandakinīm imām kamalāny avamajjantī puṣkarāṇi ca bhāmini
english: "Plunge into this Mandākinī as into a friend's embrace, Sītā—submerging the lotuses and water-lilies, fair one."

sanskrit: tvaṃ paurajanavad vyālān ayodhyām iva parvatam manyasva vanite nityaṃ sarayūvad imāṃ nadīm
english: "Consider the wild beasts like the townspeople, dear one; consider the mountain like Ayodhyā; consider this river always as the Sarayū."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaś caiva dharmātmā mannideśe vyavasthitaḥ tvaṃ cānukūlā vaidehi prītiṃ janayatho mama
english: "And virtuous-souled Lakṣmaṇa stands ever at my command; you too are devoted to me, Vaidehī—both of you fill me with joy."

sanskrit: upaspṛśaṃs triṣavaṇaṃ madhumūlaphalāśanaḥ nāyodhyāyai na rājyāya spṛhaye 'dya tvayā saha
english: "Bathing at the three sacred hours, subsisting on honey, roots, and fruits—dwelling with you now, I do not yearn for Ayodhyā, nor for the kingdom."

sanskrit: imāṃ hi ramyāṃ gajayūthalolitāṃ nipītatoyāṃ gajasiṃhavānaraiḥ supuṣpitaiḥ puṣpadharair alaṃkṛtāṃ na so 'sti yaḥ syān na gatakramaḥ sukhī
english: "There is no one who, seeing this charming river—stirred by herds of elephants, her waters drunk by elephants, lions, and monkeys, adorned with trees bearing abundant blossoms—would not feel his step gone easy and be content."

sanskrit: itīva rāmo bahusaṃgataṃ vacaḥ priyā sahāyaḥ saritaṃ prati bruvan cacāra ramyaṃ nayanāñjanaprabhaṃ sa citrakūṭaṃ raghuvaṃśavardhanaḥ
english: Speaking thus many gathered words to his beloved companion, directed toward the river, he—the increaser of the Raghu lineage—roamed through that charming Citrakūṭa, radiant as collyrium to the eyes.

sanskrit: tathā tatrāsatas tasya bharatasyopayāyinaḥ sainya reṇuś ca śabdaś ca prādurāstāṃ nabhaḥ spṛśau
english: While he dwelt there, as Bharata approached, the dust and the sound of his army rose up, touching the sky.

sanskrit: etasminn antare trastāḥ śabdena mahatā tataḥ arditā yūthapā mattāḥ sayūthā dudruvur diśaḥ
english: In that moment, terrified by the great noise, the maddened bull-elephants, tormented, fled in all directions with their herds.

sanskrit: sa taṃ sainyasamudbhūtaṃ śabdaṃ śuśrava rāghavaḥ tāṃś ca vipradrutān sarvān yūthapān anvavaikṣata
english: Rāghava heard that sound arising from the army, and he watched as all those bull-elephants scattered and fled.

sanskrit: tāṃś ca vidravato dṛṣṭvā taṃ ca śrutvā sa niḥsvanam uvāca rāmaḥ saumitriṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dīptatejasaṃ
english: Seeing them scatter in flight and hearing that sound, Rāma spoke to Saumitri, the blazing-vigoured Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: hanta lakṣmaṇa paśyeha sumitrā suprajās tvayā bhīmastanitagambhīras tumulaḥ śrūyate svanaḥ
english: "Look here, Lakṣmaṇa—Sumitrā is blessed to have such a son as you! A tumultuous sound is heard, deep as terrible thunder."

sanskrit: rājā vā rājamātro vā mṛgayām aṭate vane anyad vā śvāpadaṃ kiṃ cit saumitre jñātum arhasi sarvam etad yathātattvam acirāj jñātum arhasi
english: "Is a king or a royal prince ranging the forest in the hunt, or is it some other wild beast, O Saumitri? You must ascertain the truth of all this—discover it quickly, as it really is."

sanskrit: sa lakṣmaṇaḥ saṃtvaritaḥ sālam āruhya puṣpitam prekṣamāṇo diśaḥ sarvāḥ pūrvāṃ diśam avaikṣata
english: Lakṣmaṇa, swift to act, climbed a flowering Śala tree, and scanning all directions, he gazed to the east.

sanskrit: udaṅmukhaḥ prekṣamāṇo dadarśa mahatīṃ camūm rathāśvagajasaṃbādhāṃ yattair yuktāṃ padātibhiḥ
english: Looking northward, he discerned a great army—crowded with chariots, horses, and elephants, joined with alert foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: tām aśvagajasaṃpūrṇāṃ rathadhvajavibhūṣitām śaśaṃsa senāṃ rāmāya vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: He reported to Rāma that army filled with horses and elephants, adorned with chariot-banners, and spoke these words:

sanskrit: agniṃ saṃśamayatv āryaḥ sītā ca bhajatāṃ guhām sajyaṃ kuruṣva cāpaṃ ca śarāṃś ca kavacaṃ tathā
english: "Let the noble one extinguish the fire; let Sītā take shelter in the cave; string your bow, and take up your arrows and armour as well."

sanskrit: taṃ rāmaḥ puruṣavyāghro lakṣmaṇaṃ pratyuvāca ha aṅgāvekṣasva saumitre kasyaitāṃ manyase camūm
english: Rāma, that tiger among men, replied to Lakṣmaṇa: "Observe the insignia, Saumitri—whose army do you think this is?"

sanskrit: evam ukktas tu rāmeṇa lakṣmāṇo vākyam abravīt didhakṣann iva tāṃ senāṃ ruṣitaḥ pāvako yathā
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa spoke his words—enraged, as though wishing to burn that army like an angry fire.

sanskrit: saṃpannaṃ rājyam icchaṃs tu vyaktaṃ prāpyābhiṣecanam āvāṃ hantuṃ samabhyeti kaikeyyā bharataḥ sutaḥ
english: "Desiring the secure kingdom, and clearly having now obtained his consecration, Bharata, Kaikeyī's son, is coming to kill us both."

sanskrit: eṣa vai sumahāñ śrīmān viṭapī saṃprakāśate virājaty udgataskandhaḥ kovidāra dhvajo rathe
english: "That very great and resplendent tree shines forth—the Kovidāra banner with its upraised trunk blazes on his chariot."

sanskrit: bhajanty ete yathākāmam aśvān āruhya śīghragān ete bhrājanti saṃhṛṣṭā gajān āruhya sādinaḥ
english: "Some mounted on swift horses ride at will; others, glittering and exultant, the riders mounted on elephants, shine forth."

sanskrit: gṛhītadhanuṣau cāvāṃ giriṃ vīra śrayāvahe atha vehaiva tiṣṭhāvaḥ saṃnaddhāv udyatāyudhau api nau vaśam āgacchet kovidāradhvajo raṇe
english: "With bows in hand, let us two take to the mountain, O hero—or let us stand right here, armoured and weapons raised, so that he of the Kovidāra banner may come under our power in battle."

sanskrit: api drakṣyāmi bharataṃ yatkṛte vyasanaṃ mahat tvayā rāghava saṃprāptaṃ sītayā ca mayā tathā
english: "I shall look upon that Bharata, on account of whom such great calamity has befallen you, Rāghava, and Sītā, and me alike."

sanskrit: yannimittaṃ bhavān rājyāc cyuto rāghava śāśvatīm saṃprāpto 'yam arir vīra bharato vadhya eva me
english: "This enemy Bharata, on whose account you, Rāghava, have been deprived of the eternal kingdom—he is fit to be slain by me, O hero."

sanskrit: bharatasya vadhe doṣaṃ nāhaṃ paśyāmi rāghava pūrvāpakāriṇāṃ tyāge na hy adharmo vidhīyate etasmin nihate kṛtsnām anuśādhi vasuṃdharām
english: "I see no fault in slaying Bharata, Rāghava—for in abandoning those who have first done harm, no unrighteousness is ordained. Once he is slain, rule the entire earth."

sanskrit: adya putraṃ hataṃ saṃkhye kaikeyī rājyakāmukā mayā paśyet suduḥkhārtā hastibhagnam iva drumam
english: "Today let Kaikeyī, who craved the kingdom, see her son slain in battle by me—struck down with deep agony, like a tree shattered by an elephant."

sanskrit: kaikeyīṃ ca vadhiṣyāmi sānubandhāṃ sabāndhavām kaluṣeṇādya mahatā medinī parimucyatām
english: "And I shall slay Kaikeyī together with her partisans and kinsmen. Let the earth today be freed from this great pollution."

sanskrit: adyamaṃ saṃyataṃ krodham asatkāraṃ ca mānada mokṣyāmi śatrusainyeṣu kakṣeṣv iva hutāśanam
english: "Today I shall release this pent-up wrath and the dishonour shown to the giver of honour upon the enemy's army, like fire upon dry grass."

sanskrit: adyaitac citrakūṭasya kānanaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ bhindañ śatruśarīrāṇi kariṣye śoṇitokṣitam
english: "Today I shall drench this forest of Citrakūṭa with blood, piercing the bodies of enemies with my sharp arrows."

sanskrit: śarair nirbhinnahṛdayān kuñjarāṃs turagāṃs tathā śvāpadāḥ parikarṣantu narāś ca nihatān mayā
english: "Let the jackals and wild beasts drag away the elephants and horses whose hearts have been pierced by my arrows, and likewise the men I have slain."

sanskrit: śarāṇāṃ dhanuṣaś cāham anṛṇo 'smi mahāvane sasainyaṃ bharataṃ hatvā bhaviṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Having slain Bharata together with his army in this great forest, I shall have discharged my debt to my arrows and my bow—of this there is no doubt."
